title: Nozick's Experience Machine
rootClaim: Human beings should refuse to plug into Robert Nozick's Experience Machine because subjective pleasure is not the sole intrinsic good of human existence.

branches.text: Value of Real Contact: We care about actually doing certain things and being a certain way in objective reality, not merely experiencing the subjective sensation of having done them.

children.text: Plugging into the machine is a form of suicide of agency; it transforms the subject into a passive vessel float in a tank dependent on machine simulation.
Epistemic Indistinguishability: If the simulation is perfectly indistinguishable from reality, the subjective quality of experience and moral emotional depth are functionally identical.
Status Quo Bias Explanation: Felipe De Brigard's empirical experiments reveal that people reject plugging in primarily due to status quo bias rather than a intrinsic desire for reality.
Reverse Thought Experiment: If told they are already plugged into an Experience Machine, a majority of subjects choose to stay plugged in, validating status quo bias.
Character & Moral Growth: Authentic character development requires overcoming genuine risk, adversity, and potential failure in a shared physical world.

branches.text: Hedonist Defense: Qualitative subjective well-being is the only intrinsically valuable state; rejecting simulated bliss for 'real suffering' is irrational essentialism.

children.text: Quantitative Utilitarianism: Eliminating illness, heartbreak, and trauma via optimal simulated experience maximizes global utility far beyond natural biological limits.
Delusional Solipsism: Life in the machine removes genuine connection with other autonomous minds, reducing relationships to empty algorithmic projections.
Multi-User Network Machine: If billions of real human consciousnesses plug into a shared networked simulation, social interactions remain genuinely authentic and interactive.

definitions.description: A thought experiment proposed by Robert Nozick in 1974 to refute psychological and ethical hedonism.
An emotional preference for the current state of affairs, where any change from the baseline is perceived as a potential loss.
The philosophical theory that pleasure is the highest good and proper aim of human life.
A state where two conditions or environments cannot be differentiated by an observer using internal subjective perception alone.
